title: Experiment 9 – Client-Server Socket Programming in Java
description: Two-way client-server socket communication implementation in Java using ServerSocket and Socket classes over TCP.
aim: To write a client-server socket program using TCP in Java for two-way communication.
theory: A Network Socket is one endpoint of a two-way communication link between two programs over a computer network. The ServerSocket class binds to a local port and awaits client connections via accept(). The Socket class establishes connection to the server IP and port. Java streams (BufferedReader, PrintWriter) handle bidirectional character and data transmission.
algorithm: Invoke serverSocket.accept() to block and wait for client connection.
On client, create Socket(host, port) to perform TCP three-way handshake.
Bind BufferedReader and PrintWriter streams to socket input and output streams.
Client sends string message; Server receives, logs, and echoes back uppercase response.
When client sends termination signal (exit), cleanly close streams and socket handles.
